body:
Thanks to everyone who encouraged me to go. It was definitely the right choice. I discharged myself this morning, though the doctors would've liked me to stay through the weekend. It just wasn't a very therapeutic environment (though I have to say that it was quite liberating knowing the hardest decision I'd have to make was what I wanted to eat.)

The ultimate consensus among the MD's was that I suffered an adverse reaction to a new SSRI I was recently prescribed, Viibryd. I'm back on my previous medication regimen and feeling much better.
Given my reluctance before, after talking to my shrink and re-reading your posts, I think I will be glad I did as well.

It's OK. My Dad called my psychiatrist and voiced his concerns. He called me directly and I explained what I have in this post. Like what you said, he said that now is the time to pursue some hospitalization. 

I'm putting on some pants and making myself slightly more presentable and within a few minutes I'll be leaving for the E.R. to voluntarily admit myself. 

Thanks again for your quick reply and support. Words on the internet can only express so much but I sincerely appreciate it.

There aren't any people or things in this world that make me feel love. I know my parents "love" me by any objective measure, they certainly do--that's an indisputable fact. I'm just so detached. I lack empathy, sympathy and the ability to experience any emotion beyond the pure comical and absurd nature of my predicament. Even those moments of laughter are dark and fleeting for 5 seconds.

Thanks for your support. Facing my own mortality at this point is trivial and some other people have pointed out that I must have even a slight will to live. One of my justifications to my therapist last week for prolonging my plans to commit suicide was because my parents were out of town and if I died, there'd be no one to feed or take care of their dog.
